trip.title: Route 66 West — January
trip.subtitle: Tulsa · Cadillac Ranch · Santa Fe · Petrified Forest · Canyon de Chelly · Monument Valley · Grand Canyon · Oatman · Death Valley · Santa Monica
trip.summary: Fifteen days one way, from Dallas to the end of Route 66 on Santa Monica Pier. North to Tulsa to find the old road, then west across Oklahoma, the Texas Panhandle and New Mexico on it — Cadillac Ranch, the 1926 road into Santa Fe, and the only national park Route 66 runs through. It leaves the road for Canyon de Chelly, Monument Valley and the Grand Canyon, rejoins it at Williams for the longest empty stretch left, through Seligman, Oatman and Amboy, and swings north to Death Valley before the last run into Los Angeles. 2,611 miles, no road driven twice, and cold for the first nine nights.

itinerary.headline: Fly in, then US-75 all the way north
itinerary.notes: Land, collect the vehicle and point it north. US-75 runs from Dallas to Tulsa without a toll — the faster turnpike route bills you through the hire company — and crosses the Red River into Oklahoma about an hour out. It is the longest first day of any route on this site that starts with a flight, and you arrive after dark, which in Tulsa in January is about half past five. Keep the evening small: the Meadow Gold sign lit up on 11th Street, which is Route 66, and dinner. Tulsa: highs around 9°C, lows around −2°C.
activities: The Meadow Gold sign on 11th Street after dark
The Golden Driller at Expo Square

itinerary.headline: The best 150 miles of old 66 in Oklahoma
itinerary.notes: Slow on purpose. East first to the Blue Whale at Catoosa, then back through Tulsa and west on the two-lane that runs beside the Turner Turnpike rather than on it — Sapulpa, Kellyville, Bristow, Depew — for lunch at the Rock Café in Stroud. Then the Route 66 Interpretive Center in Chandler's 1937 armory, the Round Barn at Arcadia, and the 66-foot soda bottle at Pops. It is a Sunday, which is the catch: Chandler opens only from 1 to 5, and that is exactly when you pass. Oklahoma City: highs around 10°C, lows around −2°C.
activities: Lunch at the Rock Café, Stroud

itinerary.headline: Into the Panhandle, and Cadillacs at sunset
itinerary.notes: I-40 replaced Route 66 out here and mostly runs on top of it, so this is interstate with stops. Skip Clinton's museum — it is shut on Mondays in winter and for the first week of January — and use the National Route 66 Museum at Elk City, 25 miles on, which is open. Then the U-Drop Inn at Shamrock, the 1936 art deco Conoco station that became Ramone's in Cars, and Groom's water tower, tilted on purpose in 1980 to pull drivers off the interstate. Reach Cadillac Ranch for the last hour of light — sunset is about 5:55 — and bring a can of spray paint, because everyone does. Amarillo: highs around 10°C, lows around −5°C.
activities: The Leaning Tower of Britten, Groom

itinerary.headline: New Mexico, and the 1926 road into Santa Fe
itinerary.notes: You gain an hour at the New Mexico line. Tucumcari's motel strip first — the Blue Swallow's sign is worth the stop even by day — then the Blue Hole at Santa Rosa, a spring 80 feet deep and the colour of a swimming pool, where divers train all winter. From Santa Rosa this route leaves I-40 and takes US-84 north through Dilia to Romeroville, then I-25 over Glorieta Pass: that was Route 66 from 1926 until 1937, when it was straightened through Albuquerque. Santa Fe by mid-afternoon, for the Plaza, the Native artisans under the portal of the Palace of the Governors, and Loretto Chapel's staircase before it closes. Meow Wolf is shut on Tuesdays, so it is tomorrow morning. Santa Fe sits at 7,200 feet: highs around 7°C, lows around −6°C.
activities: The 1926 alignment through Dilia and Romeroville
Santa Fe Plaza and the Palace of the Governors

itinerary.headline: Meow Wolf at ten, Gallup by dusk
itinerary.notes: Meow Wolf's House of Eternal Return opens at 10: a Victorian house you leave through the fridge and the dryer, and more than seventy rooms beyond it. Two hours is about right, three if they are hooked. Then I-25 down to Albuquerque and I-40 west, which is the 1937 alignment. Central Avenue is Route 66 through the middle of Albuquerque, and the KiMo Theatre is ten minutes off the interstate if you want it. Gallup by about five, as the light goes. El Rancho, built in 1937 for the film crews making Westerns, is worth walking into even if you are not staying. Gallup is 6,500 feet up: highs around 8°C, lows around −6°C.
activities: Meow Wolf's House of Eternal Return, from 10

itinerary.headline: The only national park on Route 66
itinerary.notes: The short day, and the one to spend slowly. Petrified Forest is open 8 to 5 in winter, and opens late when the road is icy. Come in from I-40 at the north end: the Painted Desert overlooks, the Painted Desert Inn, and the pullout where a line of telephone poles and a rusted 1932 Studebaker mark where Route 66 crossed the park. South from there past the Newspaper Rock petroglyphs, the Blue Mesa loop — a mile's walk down among blue and purple badlands — and Agate Bridge, and out past the Giant Logs behind the Rainbow Forest Museum. 28 miles of park road; allow three or four hours. Then Holbrook and the Wigwam Motel, fifteen concrete teepees with old cars parked outside. Holbrook: highs around 11°C, lows around −7°C.
activities: The Painted Desert overlooks and the Painted Desert Inn
The Route 66 pullout and its Studebaker

itinerary.headline: Across the Navajo Nation to the Mittens
itinerary.notes: North on US-191 through Ganado and Chinle, which is paved all the way — not the shortcut across the Hopi mesas that a phone may suggest, which runs on Navajo and BIA dirt roads that are mud in January. Hubbell Trading Post at Ganado has traded with Navajo families since 1878 and is still a working store; it is free. At Chinle, Canyon de Chelly's South Rim Drive runs 18 miles out to Spider Rock, an 800-foot sandstone spire, past the White House Overlook above a cliff dwelling. It is free, but it adds about 36 miles and two hours, so this is a long day. Then 110 miles to Monument Valley for sunset over the Mittens at about 5:25. The Valley Drive's last entry in winter is 2:30, so the loop is tomorrow. Monument Valley: highs around 6°C, lows around −7°C.
activities: Canyon de Chelly South Rim Drive: White House Overlook and Spider Rock

itinerary.headline: The Valley Drive at eight, the Grand Canyon by four
itinerary.notes: Be at the gate when it opens at 8. The 17-mile Valley Drive is graded dirt — slow and bumpy, fine when dry — and takes about two and a half hours with John Ford's Point and the Three Sisters. Out by 11, then back through Kayenta, where the Burger King has long kept a small exhibit on the Navajo Code Talkers (worth ten minutes if it is still up), Tuba City and Cameron, whose 1916 trading post does a proper lunch. The Little Colorado River Gorge overlook on AZ-64 is a Navajo tribal park at $8 a head, with a sheer drop of about a thousand feet. You enter the Grand Canyon at Desert View, the best first look there is, and reach the Village as the light goes. It is Martin Luther King weekend. Grand Canyon Village: highs around 5°C, lows around −8°C.
activities: The Valley Drive at 8: John Ford's Point and the Three Sisters
Little Colorado River Gorge ($8 a head)
Sunset at Yavapai or Mather Point

itinerary.headline: The rim, and Hermit Road in your own car
itinerary.notes: The whole day on the South Rim. Sunrise at Mather Point is about 7:30. The Yavapai Geology Museum is heated and gives the best explanation of what you are looking at. The Rim Trail is paved and flat from Mather Point to the Village. The Bright Angel Trail drops straight off the edge — go down to the first switchbacks and turn round, and wear traction if it is icy. From December to February, and only then, Hermit Road is open to private cars under 22 feet: seven miles out to Hermits Rest, with Hopi Point for sunset. The coldest night of the trip: highs around 5°C, lows around −8°C.
activities: The top of the Bright Angel Trail
Hermit Road to Hermits Rest, sunset at Hopi Point

itinerary.headline: Back on 66 for the longest stretch left
itinerary.notes: South to Williams, the last town on Route 66 to be bypassed by the interstate — in October 1984 — and still built around it. Then Seligman, where Angel Delgadillo's barbershop started the campaign that saved the road; his family's Snow Cap drive-in is closed for the winter, but the gift shops are not. From Seligman to Kingman, 66 swings north away from I-40 on the longest unbroken stretch of the old road left anywhere: Peach Springs, Grand Canyon Caverns (a lift 21 storeys down into a dry cave, if you want it), and the Hackberry General Store with its forecourt of old cars and pumps. Kingman: highs around 13°C, lows right around freezing.

itinerary.headline: Burros, Roy's, and the empty Mojave
itinerary.notes: Route 66 climbs out of Kingman over Sitgreaves Pass — eight miles of hairpins with no shoulders — and drops into Oatman, a gold-mining town kept alive by the wild burros that wander its main street. They come to the car window; the shops sell bags of burro food and ask you to use that. You gain an hour crossing the Colorado River into California at Needles. Then I-40 to Kelbaker Road and the old road west to Roy's at Amboy, the 1938 motel and café with the sign everyone photographs; the café was being restored for the road's centennial, so check before counting on lunch there. Late lunch instead at the Bagdad Café in Newberry Springs, from the 1987 film. Barstow: highs around 16°C, lows around 2°C.

itinerary.headline: Into Death Valley the back way
itinerary.notes: West out of Barstow and north through Trona and the Panamint Valley, rather than east through Baker. It is 17 miles longer, and it means no road on this trip is driven twice, because day 14 leaves by Baker. It comes into the park over Towne Pass at 4,956 feet and drops almost 5,000 feet to Stovepipe Wells. Walk out onto the Mesquite Flat Dunes on the way through, then on to Furnace Creek, 190 feet below sea level, and Zabriskie Point for sunset at about five. Death Valley: highs around 18°C, lows around 4°C.

itinerary.headline: Below sea level, and warm
itinerary.notes: Badwater Basin is the lowest point in North America, 282 feet below sea level, and about 18°C in January. Walk out onto the salt there first, then Devil's Golf Course, Artist's Drive — a one-way loop through hills stained green and pink — and the easy walk up Golden Canyon. End the day at Dante's View, 5,475 feet straight above Badwater. The park is still repairing flood damage, so check its conditions page the week before. Highs around 18°C, lows around 4°C.

itinerary.headline: The last of Route 66, and the Pacific
itinerary.notes: The longest day, so leave by seven. Out past Zabriskie Point and Death Valley Junction to Baker and its 134-foot thermometer, then I-15 through Barstow and down Cajon Pass into the Los Angeles basin. Route 66's own line across the valley is Foothill Boulevard, thirty miles of traffic lights past the Wigwam Motel in Rialto; this route takes the parallel I-210 and rejoins 66 on Colorado Boulevard in Pasadena. From there the Arroyo Seco Parkway — America's first freeway, opened in 1940 and still with stop-sign on-ramps — carries it into downtown, and I-10 runs to the ocean. Aim to be past Pasadena before two, when the Friday traffic builds. The pier at dusk, with the Ferris wheel lit. Santa Monica: highs around 18°C, lows around 9°C.

itinerary.headline: The End of the Trail sign, then home
itinerary.notes: Walk out to the End of the Trail sign first thing, before the pier fills up — the photograph every Route 66 trip ends with. The legal end of the road is a mile inland, at Lincoln and Olympic, and nobody photographs that. Then nine miles to LAX. The car goes back at the airport; the motorhome goes back to Carson, which changes the morning.
activities: The End of the Trail sign

practical_notes.booking_order: The Grand Canyon first, because nights 8 and 9 fall on Martin Luther King weekend — the in-park lodges and Trailer Village before anything else. Then Monument Valley for night 7, at The View or Goulding's, then the Wigwam Motel for night 6, which has fifteen wigwams in all. In the motorhome, add Dockweiler RV Park for night 14: it takes bookings no more than 90 days ahead, which for 22 January means late October. Everything else on this route has slack in January.
practical_notes.freezing: On the January averages every night from Tulsa (−2°C) to the Grand Canyon (−8°C) goes below freezing, with Oklahoma City, Amarillo, Santa Fe, Gallup, Holbrook and Monument Valley in between. Kingman on night 10 is a coin toss at around 0°C. After that it is Barstow at 2°C, Death Valley at 4°C and Santa Monica at 9°C. Pack for a winter trip that turns into a mild one, not the other way round.
practical_notes.freeze_damage: Hire companies treat a split pipe as your damage, and El Monte's own conditions list damage caused by freezing among the things its cover never pays for, whichever cover you buy. A rig hired near Dallas will not be winterized — which you need, because you are living in it — and it drives straight into nine nights below freezing. Run the propane furnace, not the heat pump, which gives up around 4°C; disconnect the city-water hose at night and run off the fresh tank; use the tank heaters if it has them. Get it in writing that the water system is live and that the company knows where you are taking it.
practical_notes.tolls: Leaving Dallas, the Dallas North Tollway, the Bush Turnpike and the Sam Rayburn Tollway are all cashless, and so is Oklahoma's Indian Nation Turnpike. The hire company pays them and bills you with a daily fee on top, which can turn a few dollars of toll into $20 to $40. US-75 from Dallas to Tulsa is free and takes about half an hour longer, and the map shows it. Day 2 runs the old road beside the Turner Turnpike rather than on it, and from Oklahoma City to the Pacific there is no toll road on the route.
practical_notes.closed_days: The Oklahoma Route 66 Museum in Clinton closes on Sundays and Mondays from November to January, and for the first week of January — day 3 is a Monday, so this route uses the National Route 66 Museum at Elk City instead, which is open. Meow Wolf in Santa Fe closes on Tuesdays, which is day 4, so it moves to Wednesday morning. Delgadillo's Snow Cap in Seligman closes for the winter. Two more only just work: the Chandler Interpretive Center opens from 1 to 5 on Sundays, and the U-Drop Inn is shut on Sundays but you pass it on a Monday. Move the dates and all of this moves with them.
practical_notes.long_day: 311 miles and six and a half hours from Death Valley to Santa Monica, arriving on a Friday. Leave Furnace Creek by seven and aim to be through Pasadena before two, when the weekend traffic starts. If you are running late, nothing on this day has a closing time except the traffic — the pier is open into the evening on Fridays. The Wigwam Motel in Rialto would split the day in two, if the flight home allows it.
practical_notes.snow: This route crosses the Continental Divide on I-40 east of Gallup at about 7,250 feet, climbs I-25 over Glorieta Pass into Santa Fe at about 7,400, sleeps at 6,800 at the Grand Canyon and drives AZ-64 past Desert View at 7,400. A January storm can shut any of them for hours, and US-191 and US-160 across the Navajo Nation are ploughed slowly. Check nmroads.com and az511.gov the night before each of days 4 to 10. Day 6 is only 118 miles: if the weather costs you half a day, that is where it goes.
practical_notes.monument_valley: You arrive at about four on day 7, after the Valley Drive's last entry at 2:30, so the first evening is sunset from the rim. Drive the loop when the gate opens at 8 the next morning and you are out by 11, with time to reach the Grand Canyon before dark. The parts beyond the self-drive loop — Mystery Valley, Hunts Mesa, the arches — are open only with a Navajo guide, about $79 an adult and $59 a child for two and a half hours.
practical_notes.time_zones: You gain an hour at the New Mexico line on day 4 and another crossing the Colorado River into California on day 11. Every summer the Navajo Nation keeps daylight saving and the rest of Arizona does not, and visitors miss their tour times by an hour. In January nobody is on daylight saving and the clocks agree.
practical_notes.park_pass: Petrified Forest ($25), the Grand Canyon ($35) and Death Valley ($30) come to $90 at the gates, against $80 for the annual America the Beautiful pass. Monument Valley and the Little Colorado River Gorge are Navajo tribal parks at $8 to $10 a head and do not take it. Canyon de Chelly and Hubbell Trading Post are free.
practical_notes.fuel: California fuel costs more than a dollar a gallon above Arizona's. Fill up in Kingman before day 11 and again in Barstow before Death Valley, where the pumps at Furnace Creek and Stovepipe Wells are the dearest on the trip. Roy's at Amboy sells fuel, but at Amboy prices. On the Navajo Nation, fill up in Chinle or Kayenta rather than hoping for something in between.
practical_notes.death_valley: As of 2026, Lower Wildrose Road, Darwin Falls Road and Titus Canyon were closed after floods, and South Badwater Road had reopened with missing pavement and soft shoulders. None of those is on this route, but the list changes after every storm: check the park's conditions page the week before. Day 12 comes in over Panamint Valley Road and Towne Pass, which were open.
practical_notes.pickup_windows: El Monte's Dallas depot is in McKinney, 30 miles up US-75 — on day 1's road — and is open Monday to Saturday, 9 to 4, and shut on Sundays. Standard pickup is after 1pm, earlier for a fee, and the handover takes one to two hours. Returns are in the morning — 9 to 10:30 at McKinney — and the Los Angeles yard is in Santa Fe Springs, 23 miles from LAX. So day 1 leaves at about 3, and day 15 needs a flight after about 1pm.
practical_notes.valley_drive_car: Most hire agreements exclude unpaved roads, so the 17-mile Valley Drive — which families drive in hire cars every day — is at your own risk if something breaks. Go slowly, stay on the loop, and don't try it after rain or snow; the guided tour is the fallback.

money_savers.item: Collect the car in town, not at the airport
money_savers.detail: Airport counters add a concession recovery fee of around 11 per cent plus a daily facility charge. If the quote is from DFW or Love Field, price the same van from a neighbourhood branch nearby — a short taxi ride with the luggage — and dropping at LAX does not usually add the fees back.

The Dallas tollways and the Indian Nation Turnpike are cashless, and the hire company adds a daily fee to every toll it passes on. US-75 is free and about half an hour slower. After day 1 there is nothing to pay anywhere on the route.

money_savers.item: Sleep in Tusayan, not the Village
money_savers.detail: Tusayan is seven miles south of the rim, and on Martin Luther King weekend the in-park lodges are at their January high. Hermit Road and sunset at Hopi Point are the same either way.

money_savers.item: Stovepipe Wells, not The Ranch at Furnace Creek
money_savers.detail: Stovepipe Wells is inside the park, beside the dunes day 12 arrives at, and roughly half the price of The Ranch in peak season, which January is. Badwater is 25 miles further away each morning.

money_savers.item: Drive the Monument Valley loop yourself
money_savers.detail: In the car the 17-mile Valley Drive is included in the tribal entry. The guided tour is only needed for the closed parts — Mystery Valley and the arches — or if you would rather not take a hire car onto dirt.

money_savers.item: Buy the park pass at Petrified Forest
money_savers.detail: Three gates at $25, $35 and $30 against $80 for the pass. It barely pays on this route, but it also covers Wupatki, Walnut Canyon and anything else federal you add.

money_savers.item: Ride the Ferris wheel, skip the wristband
money_savers.detail: Pacific Park's unlimited-ride wristbands are priced for a day. For an hour on the pier at dusk, single tickets for the Ferris wheel and the roller coaster are a fraction of it.

money_savers.saving: ~$50 in the van, ~$150 in the motorhome
money_savers.detail: California fuel runs more than a dollar a gallon over Arizona's. Leave Kingman on a full tank on day 11 and time the next fill for Barstow rather than the Death Valley pumps.

money_savers.item: In the motorhome, pay for the extra miles, not unlimited
money_savers.detail: El Monte's unlimited mileage is $1,135 for a hire this long. The plan needs about 1,200 miles over the 1,700 included, which at $30 for each 100 comes to about $390.

money_savers.item: The Gold Package, not Peace of Mind on its own
money_savers.detail: El Monte's Peace of Mind add-on is $15 a night, $210 for this trip. The Gold Package is $119 for the whole hire and includes Peace of Mind, the awning and additional drivers, which are otherwise $6 a night each. With VIP Plus you may not need it at all; if you do, buy it that way.

El Monte sells unlimited toll coverage at $5.95 to $19.95 a night. The motorhome never meets a toll: US-75 from McKinney to Tulsa, old 66 beside the Turner Turnpike, and nothing at all west of Oklahoma City.

rejected_alternatives.reason: It would not take a motorhome one way from Dallas to Los Angeles for these dates. El Monte would, from its depot in McKinney on day 1's road.
Owners on RVshare and Outdoorsy can allow a one-way trip, but they charge about $2 a mile to fetch it back from Los Angeles — more than the hire itself on a route this long.

rejected_alternatives.place: The Oklahoma Route 66 Museum in Clinton
rejected_alternatives.reason: Closed on Sundays and Mondays from November to January, and for the first week of January — day 3 is a Monday. The National Route 66 Museum at Elk City, 25 miles further on, is open Monday to Saturday all winter.

rejected_alternatives.place: A rest day in Monument Valley
rejected_alternatives.reason: It would have cost Petrified Forest and the Wigwam Motel, and those won. With a day there you would have sunrise and sunset, a guided tour into Mystery Valley and the Wildcat Trail. As planned it is sunset, sleep and the Valley Drive.

It sits at 5,300 feet rather than 7,200, a few degrees warmer, with the neon of the 1937 alignment on Central Avenue and the Sandia Peak tramway. Santa Fe won for the Plaza, the 1926 road and Meow Wolf. Day 5 drives straight through Albuquerque, and the KiMo Theatre is ten minutes off I-40.
The first 650 miles of Route 66, through Illinois, Missouri and thirteen miles of Kansas, would need four or five more days. This trip starts where the flights land.
Death Valley to Las Vegas is 120 miles, which would free a day — but Route 66 would stop at Barstow, the finish on Santa Monica Pier would go, and four routes on this site already end in Las Vegas.

Flagstaff is on Route 66, but the line from Monument Valley to the Grand Canyon to Williams passes west of it, and Sedona is another 30 miles south with trails that are icy in January. It needs a day that does not exist.
85 extra miles between Monument Valley and the Grand Canyon, and the Southwest Loop already has them.

rejected_alternatives.place: The Hopi mesas road from Holbrook
rejected_alternatives.reason: The obvious-looking shortcut to Monument Valley, and the one a phone may pick, runs on unpaved BIA and Navajo roads. In January mud that is a bad idea in a car and a worse one in a motorhome. Ganado and Chinle are paved and pass Canyon de Chelly.

rejected_alternatives.place: The Wigwam Motel in Rialto on night 14
rejected_alternatives.reason: The other surviving Wigwam Motel on Route 66, in the San Bernardino valley. Sleeping there would cut day 14 to about five hours and put the last of the road on the final morning — but it only works with a flight home after about 4pm.
35 miles from the finish, but a day there for six is well over $1,000 in tickets alone, and there is no day to give it.
Both are 300 miles south of the route across empty New Mexico.
The Low Desert Loop has them, and they are 100 miles south of the Mojave stretch of 66.

options.name: Car and lodging
options.tagline: A hired seven-seater, fourteen rooms, and every road open
options.summary: The build this route is designed around. A seven-seater collected in Dallas and dropped at LAX, and a room every night — which matters here, because the first nine nights are below freezing. It is also the only way to drive everything on the route: the Monument Valley loop, Hermit Road, Artist's Drive, Dante's View, Sitgreaves Pass and the Arroyo Seco are all barred to a 30-foot motorhome or no place for one. It costs more, and almost all of the gap is lodging and food.

vehicle.detail: Chrysler Pacifica · Honda Odyssey · Toyota Sienna · Chevrolet Suburban · one way, Dallas to Los Angeles
vehicle.notes: Book by seatbelt count. A minivan is better for six people for fifteen days; a Suburban is better for their luggage. Nothing on the route needs four-wheel drive, but the first week crosses country that ices overnight — ask for tyres with tread on them. Read the agreement for two things: unpaved roads, because the Monument Valley loop is graded dirt, and Sitgreaves Pass.

pros: Every road on the route is open to you: the Monument Valley loop, Hermit Road, Artist's Drive, Dante's View, Sitgreaves Pass and the Arroyo Seco.
A heated room on each of the nine freezing nights.
Parks anywhere — the Santa Fe Plaza, the Wigwam's forecourt, Santa Monica Pier.
Around $700 less fuel than the motorhome.
Collected and returned at the airports, whenever the counters are open.
cons: Lodging and food are the two biggest lines in the budget.
Three children belted in for 2,600 miles, with nowhere to move.

budget.notes: Best value sleeps in chain motels on the edge of each town, in Tusayan for the Grand Canyon and at Stovepipe Wells for Death Valley, and drives the Monument Valley loop itself. Best location sleeps on the Plaza in Santa Fe, at El Rancho, at The View in Monument Valley, inside the Grand Canyon, at The Ranch in Death Valley and by the beach in Santa Monica, and takes the Navajo-guided tour. The Wigwam Motel is the same in both.

lines.basis: Quoted: six seats, into Dallas on 9 January and home from LAX on the 23rd.
Quoted: $2,100 for a seven-seater one way, collected in Dallas on 9 January and dropped at LAX on the 23rd.

About 2,850 miles with the park roads, at around 21 mpg in a seven-seat minivan — a Suburban would add roughly $120. Around $3.00 a gallon in Texas and Oklahoma, $3.20 to $3.40 in New Mexico and Arizona and $4.80 in California, on the EIA's forecast of $3.35 nationally for 2027.
Two rooms, or a family suite, every night. The dear nights are the Grand Canyon on Martin Luther King weekend, Death Valley in its peak season, and Santa Monica on a Friday.
Six people for fifteen days: hotel breakfasts, a diner lunch on the road, dinner out.
Hotel parking in Santa Fe and Santa Monica, and a downtown night in Tulsa or Oklahoma City in the location column. Free almost everywhere else.
Covers Petrified Forest, the Grand Canyon and Death Valley — $90 at the gates.
Monument Valley at $8 to $10 a head, plus the Little Colorado River Gorge at $8 a head in the location column. The park pass is not valid at either.
Two and a half hours at about $79 an adult and $59 a child. In the value column you drive the loop yourself.
Roughly $40 an adult and $30 a child; prices vary by date.
Elk City at $5 an adult and $4 a child, and Chandler's Interpretive Center.
The Ferris wheel for six in the value column, unlimited-ride wristbands in the other.
Loretto Chapel, spray paint at Cadillac Ranch, snacks at Pops, and Grand Canyon Caverns in the location column.

options.name: Motorhome
options.tagline: Cheaper, colder, and shut out of six places
options.summary: A Class C from El Monte's depot in McKinney — thirty miles up US-75, on day 1's road — returned to their yard in Santa Fe Springs, twenty miles from LAX. Cruise America would not take one this far one way; El Monte will. It is still the cheaper build, and the long Oklahoma and Texas days go easier when the children can get up and move about. But this is the hardest route on the site for a motorhome: nine freezing nights in a row with live plumbing, a 1pm handover that puts the end of day 1 in the dark, about 1,200 miles over the quote's allowance, and six places on the route where it is barred or unwise.

vehicle.detail: El Monte Class C Family Sleeper · sleeps 7 · 7 seatbelts · 30–32 ft long · about 8 mpg · one way, McKinney TX to Santa Fe Springs CA
vehicle.notes: Ask for the Family Sleeper by name: it has seven seatbelts, where El Monte's Class C Large has exactly six and is rated for four adults and two children. At 30 to 32 feet it is too long for Hermit Road's 22-foot limit and for Death Valley's 25-foot roads, as any Class C this size is. Confirm that the water system is live and the unit is not winterized: this route has nine freezing nights before it warms up.

pros: The kitchen: breakfasts and lunches in, and the long days across Oklahoma and Texas go easier when three children can get up.
Full hookups at Trailer Village, inside the Grand Canyon and a short walk from the rim.
The last night is at Dockweiler, a county campground on the beach.
cons: Nine nights below freezing in a row, with live plumbing.
Barred from the Monument Valley loop, Hermit Road, Artist's Drive and the top of Dante's View; no place for it on Sitgreaves Pass or the Arroyo Seco.
A 1pm handover in McKinney puts the end of day 1 in the dark.
Around $700 more fuel than the car.
About 1,200 miles over the 1,700 the hire includes, at $30 for each 100.

budget.notes: The hire is El Monte's quote, one way with 1,700 miles. The low column adds only the miles the plan needs, the cheapest open campground at each stop, and no guided tour or add-on. The high column allows 300 more miles, takes the Gold Package, the Monument Valley tour and the Pacific Park wristbands.

lines.basis: Quoted: six seats, into Dallas on 9 January and home from LAX on the 23rd.
Quoted by El Monte: McKinney to Santa Fe Springs, 9 to 23 January, with 1,700 miles included.

About 2,900 miles in the motorhome — the day routes, the Canyon de Chelly rim, Death Valley's side roads and ten miles a day around campgrounds and supermarkets — at $30 for each 100 over. The high column allows another 300.

lines.item: Peace of Mind, as the Gold Package
lines.basis: Only if El Monte says the VIP Plus cover does not pay for a windscreen. Then take the Gold Package, $119 for the hire with Peace of Mind, the awning and extra drivers, rather than Peace of Mind alone at $15 a night. Breakdowns and 24/7 roadside support are included either way.
About 2,900 miles at 8 to 9 mpg, on the same regional prices as the car — Texas and Oklahoma cheapest, California dearest.
